Regulatory dates.

What changes, who it affects and what to do now, from our regulatory tracker. Undated items are listed where we expect them.

BETA

Dates are checked against each funder's or organiser's own page and carry a flag: confirmed, estimated from the last cycle, or date not published. Check the source before you apply. 41 of 73 records checked on 16 November 2026; each row shows its own check date.

Get alerts: join the beta
  1. 2 December 2026

    EU AI Act: new prohibitions and synthetic-content marking apply

    Affects: Any firm offering generative AI in the EU

    Two new EU AI Act prohibitions apply: systems that generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery. Machine-readable marking of synthetic output under Article 50(2) also applies to generative systems already on the market Do now: Confirm your vendors mark synthetic output and that your own builds do too

    Full analysis
  2. December 2026 (expected)

    FINRA 2027 oversight report expected

    Affects: US broker-dealers

    FINRA's 2027 oversight report, if it follows the 2026 report's release on 9 December 2025 Do now: Re-read the 2026 report's agent section and check you can track agent actions and decisions

    Full analysis
  3. 1 January 2027

    Colorado automated decision-making law takes effect

    Affects: Developers and deployers using automated decisions in lending, insurance, employment and other covered areas for Colorado consumers

    Colorado's Automated Decision-Making Technology in Consequential Decisions Act takes effect, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act: notice before use, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, and meaningful human review on request Do now: Identify which automated decisions reach Colorado consumers; deployers keep compliance records for three years after each use

    Full analysis
  4. Q1 2027

    FCA evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort

    Affects: UK firms

    The FCA publishes its evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort: Aereve, Barclays, Coadjute, Experian, GoCardless, Lloyds Banking Group (Scottish Widows), Palindrome and UBS. Testing ends by the end of 2026 Do now: Read it for the supervisor's view of production AI in banking, payments and credit data

    Full analysis
  5. Not yet dated

    US bank regulators' request for information on AI

    Affects: US banks

    The US banking agencies' request for information on model risk and "banks' use of AI, including generative AI and agentic AI", promised in April when SR 26-2 left both out of scope. Not in the Federal Register as of 24 October 2026 Do now: Prepare your answer now: how you validate retrieval, guardrails and agent actions, and how you would stop an agent

    Full analysis
  6. Not yet dated

    Ruling on summary judgment in the publishers' copyright cases against OpenAI and Microsoft

    Affects: Anyone training or fine-tuning on third-party content

    A ruling on OpenAI's and Microsoft's summary judgment motions in the news publishers' copyright cases, including New York Times v. OpenAI. The publishers filed their opposition in October 2026; no ruling date has been set Do now: Inventory the provenance of every corpus your models touch

    Full analysis
  7. Not yet dated

    First DOJ AI Litigation Task Force lawsuit

    Affects: Firms planning around state AI laws

    The first lawsuit brought in the name of the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, created under the executive order of 11 December 2025. The DOJ intervened on 24 April 2026 in xAI's challenge to the 2024 Colorado AI Act, which Colorado then repealed and replaced Do now: Avoid building compliance around any single state regime until this settles

    Full analysis
  8. 2 August 2027

    EU AI Act: legacy general-purpose AI models must comply

    Affects: Model providers directly; firms that fine-tune or rebrand models

    General-purpose AI models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 must comply; each member state must have at least one operational AI regulatory sandbox Do now: Ask your model vendors for their compliance position and documentation

    Full analysis
  9. 2 December 2027

    EU AI Act: high-risk obligations for Annex III systems

    Affects: Lenders, insurers and employers using AI in the EU

    EU AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply, including creditworthiness and credit scoring of individuals, life and health insurance pricing, and recruitment Do now: Start conformity and logging work now; deployers must keep logs for at least six months

    Full analysis
  10. 2 August 2028

    EU AI Act: high-risk obligations for Annex I products

    Affects: Product makers, rarely financial firms

    High-risk obligations for AI built into products regulated under Annex I apply Do now: Note it; little action for most financial firms

    Full analysis
